grammar.title: Squeezed words: I'm · you'll · it's · I'd
grammar.pattern: I am → I'm · you will → you'll · it is / it has → it's · I would / I had → I'd
grammar.rule: In speech, small words join the word before them. **it's** can be *it is* or *it has*; **I'd** can be *I would* or *I had* – the next word tells you which.
examples: It's been a long day. (= it has)
I'd better go. (= I had)
I'd love a coffee. (= I would)
grammar.vi: Dạng rút gọn – nghe kỹ âm cuối /m/, /l/, /s/, /d/.

mistake.tip: The /d/ is very short, but it's there.

grammar.title: be used to + V-ing  vs  used to + V
grammar.pattern: be/get used to + V-ing / noun  ·  used to + base verb
grammar.rule: **be used to** = it is normal for you now. **get used to** = it is becoming normal. **used to + V** = you did it in the past, not now.
examples: I'm used to getting up early.
You'll get used to the rain.
I used to live in Hanoi.
grammar.vi: be used to + V-ing = đã quen với · used to + V = đã từng (giờ không còn).

mistake.wrong: I'm not used to get up early.
mistake.right: I'm not used to getting up early.
mistake.tip: In 'be used to', 'to' is a preposition → V-ing.

practice.q: I'm slowly getting used to ___ (walk) in the rain.
When I was a kid, I ___ (play) football every day.

grammar.title: Verb + -ing  or  verb + to-infinitive
grammar.pattern: suggest / enjoy / finish / mind + V-ing  ·  decide / want / hope / plan + to V
grammar.rule: Some verbs are followed by **-ing**, others by **to + verb**. Learn them as chunks: *suggest doing*, *decide to do*.
examples: She suggested taking the tram.
I enjoy listening to podcasts.
He decided to leave early.

mistake.wrong: He suggested to take a taxi.

practice.q: My friend suggested ___ (listen) to a podcast.

grammar.title: It takes + time  vs  spend + time
grammar.pattern: It takes (sb) + time + to V  ·  sb spends + time + V-ing
grammar.rule: **It takes** focuses on the time needed. **Spend** focuses on the person using the time.
examples: It takes twenty minutes to walk there.
It took me an hour to log in.
He spent an hour logging in.
grammar.vi: It takes … to V = mất bao lâu · spend … V-ing = dành thời gian làm.

mistake.wrong: I spent an hour to log in.
mistake.right: I spent an hour logging in.

practice.q: It ___ me ten minutes to find the café.
She spends a lot of time ___ (read).

grammar.title: Contrast: although · even though · however · yet · though
grammar.pattern: Although + clause, clause.  ·  Sentence. However, sentence.  ·  …, yet …  ·  …, though.
grammar.rule: All show a **turn** in the idea. **Although/even though** join two parts in one sentence. **However** starts a new sentence + comma. **Yet** = but (surprising). **though** can end a sentence.
examples: Although he was tired, he helped.
The answer sounded right. However, it was wrong.
It's small, yet it's always full.
The coffee is great, though.
grammar.vi: Từ nối đối lập: mặc dù / tuy nhiên / vậy mà / dù vậy.

mistake.wrong: Although he was tired, but he helped.
mistake.right: Although he was tired, he helped.

practice.q: ___ it was raining, we went for a walk.
It looked easy. ___, it took three hours.

grammar.title: unless = if … not
grammar.rule: **Unless** sets a condition: the result happens only if the condition is NOT true. Don't confuse it with *although* (a surprising fact).
examples: I can't sleep unless it's dark. (= if it's not dark, I can't sleep)
Take the tram unless you want to walk an hour.
grammar.vi: unless = trừ khi / nếu không. ≠ although (mặc dù).

mistake.wrong: Unless it was raining, we went out. (= although)
mistake.right: Although it was raining, we went out.

practice.q: You won't understand it ___ you listen three times.
practice.why: = if you don't listen three times.

grammar.title: rather · rather than · instead
grammar.pattern: not A. Rather, B.  ·  B rather than A  ·  B instead of A / A. Instead, B.
grammar.rule: Use these when you say **not A – B**. *Rather* often starts the second sentence.
examples: He didn't text. Rather, he called.
I'll walk rather than take the tram.
Let's have tea instead of coffee.
grammar.vi: thay vì / thay vào đó / đúng hơn là.

mistake.wrong: I'll walk rather than taking the tram.
mistake.right: I'll walk rather than take the tram.
mistake.tip: rather than + same verb form as the first verb.

practice.q: She doesn't text much. ___, she calls.

grammar.title: had better + verb
grammar.pattern: sb had better ('d better) + base verb
grammar.rule: Strong advice: you should, or something bad may happen. Usually short: **I'd better**.
examples: It's late – I'd better go.
You'd better take an umbrella.

mistake.wrong: You had better to take an umbrella.

practice.q: It's going to rain. You'd better ___ (take) an umbrella.

grammar.title: Place words: opposite · next to · on the corner · at the end of
grammar.pattern: opposite + place · next to + place · on the corner (of …) · at the end of the street
grammar.rule: Use these to say **where** something is, especially when giving directions.
examples: The tram stop is opposite the church.
The shop is next to the bank.
There's a café on the corner.
grammar.vi: đối diện · bên cạnh · ở góc phố · ở cuối phố.

mistake.wrong: The shop is next the bank.
mistake.right: The shop is next to the bank.

practice.q: The bank and the shop are side by side. The shop is ___ the bank.

grammar.title: the rest of the · the remaining · the remainder of the
grammar.pattern: the rest of the + noun · the remaining + noun · the remainder of the + noun
grammar.rule: All mean **what is left**. *The rest of the* is the most common in speech. *Remaining* is an adjective before a noun.
examples: I'll read the rest of the story tonight.
The remaining countries agreed.

practice.q: I ate half of the pizza. I'll eat ___ ___ ___ it later.
